first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly on the iPad. It is sensible and not gushing. It tells you straight off that the ring isn't covered automatically and that travel insurance has gaps, which is exactly the sort of thing I'd nag her about anyway. I like that it says it only uses Australian government and industry sources.

journey.quote: Engagement ring insurance is not automatic.
journey.reaction: Good. Plain, practical, and it treats checking the fine print as normal rather than fussy.

journey.quote: This guide follows the ring from the counter to a proposal abroad and on to the wedding, using only public Australian sources.
journey.reaction: Moneysmart, Smartraveller, the Insurance Council. Those are names I know and trust. Far better than some blogger's opinion.

journey.section: What the PDS is, and why it matters
journey.quote: You may also see a Target Market Determination (TMD), a short document describing who the product is designed for.
journey.reaction: I don't need this one. It's one more acronym in a section already full of them. Not a big problem, I'd skim past it.

journey.section: What to check in any policy before you rely on it
journey.quote: | Question to ask | Where to look |
journey.reaction: This table is what I'd print out or forward to my husband. Questions to ask, and where to find the answer. Very useful.

journey.section: Excess, conditions and when cover starts
journey.quote: As for the moment cover begins, check your policy and get the start date in writing.
journey.reaction: Yes. Get it in writing. That's my kind of advice.

journey.section: Travelling to your destination wedding with the rings
journey.quote: Smartraveller lists what standard travel policies typically do not cover: items left unattended, items not stored in a hotel safe when one was available, items left with someone met on the trip, and items stolen from checked baggage or a locked car.
journey.reaction: Practical and specific. This is the bit I'd point out to my daughter before they fly.

journey.section: Travelling to your destination wedding with the rings
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, so the logistics around the rings sit inside one plan.
journey.reaction: A single point of contact is what I want to hear. But it's a person with no name, and it says they handle payments without a word about how deposits are held or protected. If they're touching our money overseas, I want to know who is responsible.

journey.section: If a ring is stolen overseas: police report first
journey.quote: The Australian Government cannot help with an insurance claim or replace anything other than a passport.
journey.reaction: Blunt and useful. Good to know before something goes wrong rather than after.

journey.quote: After that, the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) is a free, fair and independent service for consumers with complaints about financial firms, including insurers.
journey.reaction: Telling me where to go if it all goes wrong makes me trust the writer more. Most of these wedding sites never mention complaints.

journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor will plan the venue and the travel with you from first idea to the last dance, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD is reassuring, and working in our time zone answers my 2am question in part. 'First idea to the last dance' is a bit sales-brochure, but I can live with it.

unanswered_questions: Who do I ring if something goes wrong overseas on the day, and is that the same Wedded Advisor?
When the Advisor handles payments to overseas venues and vendors, are deposits protected, and who is responsible if a supplier disappears?
Are your fees agreed in writing before anything is booked?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before we commit to anything?
Does the Advisor help with travel insurance for the whole party, including older guests with medical conditions? The article only covers the rings.
would_share_with: My daughter and her fiancé (the travel and hotel safe section)

cta_reaction.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, so the logistics around the rings sit inside one plan.
cta_reaction.why: I'd click to see who these people are, but I wouldn't fill in a form off the back of a ring insurance article. I want to know who the person is, how deposits are handled and that I can ring them before anything is booked.

top_3_changes: Where the Advisor is said to handle payments, add one plain line on who is accountable for deposits and suppliers, or link to a page that explains it. I'm deferring to the team on the exact business detail.
Say near the CTA that you can speak to an Advisor by phone before anything is booked. People like me won't book anything from a web form.
Cut or shorten the Target Market Determination paragraph. It's one acronym too many in a section that's already heavy.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, 62, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible

open_questions: Business details (fee model, deposit protection, named Advisor, phone call before booking) are deferred per orchestrator, so the deposit point is flagged as medium, not must-fix.
assumptions: Read the whole article top to bottom, as this persona does.
Persona is provisional and not CRM-calibrated (weight 0.20).
